summary: Describes the role and responsibilities of the Independent Submission Editor, who approves documents in the Independent Submission stream. The ISE is appointed by the IAB and works with draft editors, reviewers, the RFC Production Center and Publisher, and the RFC Series Editor.

eli5.summary: This describes the job of the person who decides which outside-the-usual-route documents become RFCs.

questions: what is the independent submission editor
subtitle: The job description of the Independent Submission Editor, who approves RFCs that come from outside the IETF, IAB and IRTF.

tldr.problem: The Independent Submission stream needs a clearly defined manager, and the earlier definition referred to administrative structures that had been replaced.
tldr.mechanism: The Independent Submission Editor (ISE) is one individual, appointed by and responsible to the IAB, who reviews and approves submissions, sends approved drafts to the RFC Production Center, and is supported by a volunteer Editorial Board.
tldr.outcome: RFC 8730 obsoletes RFC 6548, replacing references to the old IASA structures with the IASA 2.0 structure.

today: RFC 8730 is an Informational RFC published in February 2020 that obsoletes RFC 6548. It has been updated by RFC 9280 and RFC 9920.

sections.title: Purpose and Background
sections.content:
The RFC Editor Model (RFC 8728) defines a set of streams that produce draft RFCs for publication. This document defines the management function for one of them, the Independent Submission stream, specifically the role of the Independent Submission Editor (ISE).

The previous version, RFC 6548, was derived from RFC 5620 and separated out from RFC 6635. This version aligns the model with the IASA 2.0 structure (RFC 8711), which creates the IETF Administration Limited Liability Company (the LLC) run by a board of directors.
sections.eli5: There are several paths for papers to become RFCs. This document is about the one path for papers from outside the usual groups, and about its boss.

sections.title: Who the ISE Is
sections.content:
The ISE is an individual responsible for the Independent Submission stream of RFCs, as defined in RFC 8729. The stream and the ISE are not under the authority or direction of the RFC Series Editor (RSE) or the RFC Series Oversight Committee (RSOC). The ISE is appointed by, and responsible directly to, the IAB, after input has been collected from the community.

The ISE is a senior position. The desired qualifications are broad technical competence, thorough familiarity with the RFC series, the ability to set up advisory and review arrangements, good standing in the technical community, demonstrated editorial skills and good command of English, and the ability to work in a multi-actor environment with divided authority.
sections.eli5: The ISE is like the editor of a school newspaper who answers to the principal rather than to the other teachers, and who needs to be good at reading and judging many kinds of writing.

sections.title: What the ISE Does
sections.content:
The ISE may have assistants and is responsible for seven things:

  1. Maintaining the technical quality of the stream.
  2. Reviewing, approving and processing Independent Submissions.
  3. Forwarding draft RFCs to the RFC Production Center.
  4. Defining and developing the scope of the stream as part of the overall RFC Editor function.
  5. Reviewing and approving errata for Independent Submissions.
  6. Coordinating work and conforming to general RFC Series policies set by the IAB and RSE.
  7. Providing statistics and documentation as requested by the RSE and the LLC.

The ISE may also choose people for an Advisory Board on special topics; it exists at the ISE's pleasure.
sections.eli5: The ISE reads submitted papers, decides which to publish, passes the winners to the printers, checks fixes to old papers, and reports to the people who run the library.

sections.title: The Editorial Board and Funding
sections.content:
The ISE is supported by the Independent Submission Editorial Board, a volunteer board that reviews stream documents. It exists at the pleasure of the ISE, and its members serve at the pleasure of the ISE. The model only notes its existence and treats further discussion as out of scope.

The ISE itself is a volunteer function. The IAB nevertheless considers maintaining the stream part of its supported activities, so the LLC should include these costs in the IASA budget.
sections.eli5: Volunteers help the editor read the papers. The editor is a volunteer too, but the library still sets aside money to support the work.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The document says it has no specific security implications. The same security considerations as those in RFC 4846 and RFC 8729 apply.
sections.eli5: Nothing new to worry about here beyond the safety rules the library already has.
